listing_note: Euronext Amsterdam ordinary listing (AEX Index constituent), reports in EUR. Same underlying company as the US OTC ADR ADYEY (1 ADS = 1/100th of one ADYEN.AS ordinary share); this file is the EUR-denominated primary-listing version, refreshed after the H1 2026 Shareholder Letter (published 13 August 2026) and subsequent analyst reaction through late August 2026.
overview: Adyen is a Dutch financial technology company that operates a single, self-built global platform combining payment acquiring, processing, risk/fraud management, and (via its own EU, US, and UK banking licenses) embedded financial products such as issuing, business accounts, and capital. It serves large enterprises and fast-growing software platforms/marketplaces (customers include Uber, Spotify, Meta, McDonald's, eBay, Etsy, Starbucks, LVMH, Toast, and Lufthansa) across three commercial pillars: Digital (online-first enterprises), Unified Commerce (combined online and in-store retail/hospitality), and Platforms (embedded payments and financial products for SaaS/marketplace businesses). In July 2026 Adyen closed its first-ever acquisitions (Talon.One, Orb), adding loyalty/promotions and usage-based billing capability and beginning a fourth, pre/post-transaction layer to the platform. Adyen operates globally with EMEA as its largest region (~55% of H1 2026 net revenue), followed by North America (~27%), APAC (~11%), and LATAM (~7%).

business_model.description: Adyen earns revenue primarily by taking a small percentage ("take rate") plus fixed fees on the total payment volume it processes for merchants, net of interchange and scheme fees passed through to card networks/issuing banks. Because it owns the full technology stack (gateway, processing, acquiring, risk engine) and its own banking licenses rather than stitching together third-party vendors, it can offer a single global integration with consistent performance, and is increasingly monetizing adjacent financial products (issuing, capital/lending, business accounts, money movement, and now loyalty/promotions via Talon.One and usage-based billing via Orb) on top of the core payments rail. Revenue is highly variable/transactional (tied to merchants' processed volume) rather than subscription-based, though the enterprise relationships themselves are extremely sticky (multi-year contracts, deep technical integration), producing recurring, compounding growth as existing customers expand usage ("land and expand"). Management disclosed in the H1 2026 letter that a typical customer's share-of-wallet scales from under 20% in years 3-7 to over 40% after year 12 — direct quantification of the land-and-expand curve. Roughly two-thirds of H1 2026 growth came from customers onboarded in 2024 and earlier; the customer base is also diversifying, with the top 300 merchants now accounting for ~60% of total growth, down from >70% three years ago. Adyen pays no dividend and conducts no share buybacks — it retains 100% of profit to reinvest in the platform (and, since July 2026, in bolt-on M&A), so unlike most large-cap compounders there is no capital-return offset to dilution/opex growth, and equity-value CAGR is driven purely by earnings/multiple, not per-share count reduction.

revenue_streams.name: Digital
revenue_streams.description: Payments for online-first enterprises: subscription/media, travel, mobility, digital marketplaces, financial services
revenue_streams.approx_share: ~55% of H1 2026 net revenue (€719.7mn, +13% YoY reported / +15% CC); processed volume €427.9bn +17% YoY. Slowest pillar again, but an improvement from Q1 2026's +9% reported/+13% CC (the slowest print in company history), driven by wallet-share gains with the largest content & subscription customers

revenue_streams.name: Unified Commerce
revenue_streams.description: Combined online and in-store payments for global retail, hospitality, food & beverage, entertainment, and travel/airlines merchants
revenue_streams.approx_share: ~32% of H1 2026 net revenue (€417.7mn, +25% YoY reported / +27% CC); processed volume €240.9bn +27% YoY; 486 customers now processing at scale (>=€10mn on both POS and e-commerce, >€50mn total volume LTM), fastest-scaling cohort of large omnichannel merchants and the natural home for the newly acquired Talon.One loyalty platform

revenue_streams.name: Platforms
revenue_streams.description: Embedded payments and financial products (issuing, capital, business accounts, and now usage-based billing via Orb) for SaaS platforms and marketplaces (e.g., eBay, Etsy, Lightspeed, Fresha)
revenue_streams.approx_share: ~13% of H1 2026 net revenue (€165.5mn, +37% YoY reported / +40% CC); processed volume €135.0bn +42% YoY; 37 platform customers now processing >€1bn annually (up from 32 a year ago); active business customers (for capital eligibility) 293K, +51% YoY — fastest-growing pillar by a wide margin and the natural home for Orb's billing infrastructure

revenue_streams.name: Net interest income
revenue_streams.description: Interest earned on merchant float/settlement balances (net interest income) plus finance income on Adyen's own cash held at central/commercial banks (reported separately below EBITDA)
revenue_streams.approx_share: Net interest income €8.6mn in H1 2026 (small, embedded within net revenue); separately, €143.2mn of finance income on own cash flowed through net income (below EBITDA) in H1 2026, down slightly from €138.7mn in H1 2025 despite a larger cash balance, reflecting a lower rate environment

business_model.customer_type: Large enterprise (B2B) merchants and platform/marketplace businesses; skews toward large, complex, multi-region customers rather than SMB. Customer base includes Uber, Spotify, Meta, McDonald's, eBay, Etsy, Starbucks, LVMH, Lufthansa, Toast (newly expanded into the U.S. in H1 2026), Tod's Group, GOV.UK Pay, On Running, Navan, iFood, Vietnam Airlines. Early agentic-commerce partners include OpenAI, American Express, Mastercard, Salesforce, and Visa.
business_model.geographic_mix: H1 2026 net revenue: EMEA €722.5mn (55%, +15% reported/+15% CC), North America €358.1mn (27%, +23% reported/+30% CC), APAC €136.9mn (11%, +23% reported/+26% CC), LATAM €85.3mn (7%, +43% reported/+35% CC). Processed volume €803.8bn in H1 2026, +24% YoY; take rate 16.2bps, down from 16.8bps in H1 2025, which management attributes to 'expected volume tiering' as large enterprise merchants scale.
business_model.balance_sheet_caveat: Adyen's reported cash balance (€12.4bn as of 30 June 2026) is overwhelmingly merchant settlement float held in transit as a licensed payment institution/bank, not discretionary shareholder capital. Own cash, excluding short-term merchant liabilities/receivables, was €4.9bn; net of the Talon.One/Orb consideration it was approximately €4.6bn. €655.2mn of the Talon.One deal sat on the 30-June balance sheet as 'prepaid acquisition consideration' pending the 1-July close. The July 2026 Talon.One (€750mn, of which €69.8mn paid in Adyen shares)/Orb ($335mn, of which $33.2mn paid in shares) deals were funded from available cash resources but represent a small fraction of the float-inflated balance sheet, not evidence of surplus capital generally being redeployed.

competitive_position.market_position: Tier-1 enterprise payments player alongside Stripe in the large-enterprise/complex-commerce segment; global market share remains modest given the massive, fragmented global payments TAM. Dominant position among large, complex, multi-channel merchants (retail, luxury, travel, marketplaces) that value a single global platform over point solutions; still building out share in North America and in the SMB/platform long tail, where Stripe is structurally stronger. Braintree (PayPal) has begun contesting Adyen's Unified Commerce turf directly by adding in-store processing for enterprise customers, a new competitive vector beyond the historical online-only overlap. The June 2026 large-merchant pricing revision, and the H1 2026 take-rate decline to 16.2bps (from 16.8bps in H1 2025), keep the pricing-power debate live even though H1 growth (24% volume, 21% CC net revenue) reaccelerated and management raised FY2026 guidance.

moat_factors.description: One codebase/platform spanning gateway, processing, acquiring and risk, avoiding the fragmented, multi-vendor architecture of legacy processors (Fiserv, FIS, Worldpay) and enabling faster feature rollout, more consistent uptime/performance, and unified data across channels — this is Adyen's core structural differentiator versus both legacy acquirers and Stripe's more modular, developer-first approach

Netherlands/EU credit institution, US Federal Foreign Branch, UK PRA/FCA licenses allow Adyen to run acquiring, issuing, accounts, and capital natively rather than through third-party bank partners. In H1 2026 Adyen added a Category II payments license from the Central Bank of the UAE and direct membership of France's STET domestic clearing system, extending direct-rail access — a regulatory barrier to entry few competitors replicate

moat_factors.factor: Unified Commerce (online + in-store on one platform)
moat_factors.description: Genuine differentiator most competitors cannot match at scale — 486 customers now processing at scale across channels (up from prior periods), with the newly acquired Talon.One explicitly pitched to bridge online/offline loyalty, a gap standalone loyalty systems cannot replicate. Legacy acquirers are typically online-only or in-store-only; Braintree's 2026 push into in-store enterprise processing is the first credible near-term threat to this pillar's exclusivity

Management now discloses the actual share-of-wallet curve: under 20% in years 3-7, over 40% after year 12 on the platform (H1 2026 letter). Roughly two-thirds of H1 2026 growth came from pre-2024 cohorts; longstanding partners (Google, Microsoft, Spotify, Uber) continue to expand usage even after a decade. Top-300-customer concentration of growth fell from >70% to ~60% over three years, evidence the base is broadening, not just deepening

Proprietary real-time risk/conversion optimization layer (Adyen Uplift) now has a quantified, disclosed benefit: +0.9 percentage points average conversion uplift by end of H1 2026, with named case studies (On Running +0.85% conversion, -0.17% fraud rate, 71,000 additional transactions in year one). Talon.One and Orb are both explicitly built on top of this same Dynamic Identification layer, extending the data advantage pre- and post-transaction rather than just at the point of sale

Talon.One (enterprise loyalty/promotions, 300+ global brands) and Orb (usage-based billing) close a portfolio of adjacent, high-switching-cost enterprise infrastructure around the core payments rail. If integration succeeds this extends the moat into pre-transaction engagement and monetization; if it fails or dilutes management attention it is a net negative — too early (deals closed 1 July 2026) to rate strength definitively

weaknesses: Take rate declined to 16.2bps in H1 2026 from 16.8bps in H1 2025 — management frames this as 'expected volume tiering' (large merchants scaling into lower marginal pricing), but this is observationally similar to what pricing pressure would also produce, and the June 2026 large-merchant pricing revision means Adyen itself has now proactively adjusted terms rather than the take rate simply drifting on mix
Concentration in a small number of very large customers, though improving: top 300 merchants now ~60% of total growth vs. >70% three years ago per the H1 2026 letter

Sub-scale in North America relative to incumbents (Fiserv, Global Payments/Worldpay, PayPal) and relative to Stripe's home-market dominance, despite North America growing fastest of all regions in H1 2026 (+30% CC) and now 27% of revenue

Digital, the largest pillar (~55% of H1 2026 revenue), remains the slowest-growing (+13% reported/+15% CC), and while this is an improvement on Q1 2026's record-low +9%/+13% CC, one half of reacceleration is not yet enough data to distinguish cyclical recovery from a structurally lower long-run growth rate for the pillar

History of repeated negative guidance/growth surprises (H1 2023 hiring-cycle miss; Feb 2026 guidance step-down; May 2026 CFO resignation; June 2026 pricing revision) shows the model can wobble materially and has produced an unusually turbulent 18-month stretch even as H1 2026 results themselves were strong

CapEx guidance raised sharply to 7% of net revenue for 2026 (from 'up to 5%'), officially framed as a one-year pull-forward of 2027 datacenter spend to lock in compute/storage pricing amid supply-chain constraints — genuine, but also a real cash cost the market had not priced, and a data point that AI-era infrastructure competition is more capital-intensive than the prior 5%-of-revenue framework assumed

business.risk: Competitive intensity from Stripe, Braintree/PayPal, Checkout.com
business.description: Stripe continues to move upmarket into large enterprise (Microsoft, Nvidia); Braintree has begun contesting Adyen's Unified Commerce differentiation directly by adding enterprise in-store processing; Checkout.com continues to compete for European online enterprise share; Adyen's own June 2026 large-merchant pricing revision is itself evidence of intensifying price competition, though the H1 2026 print (24% volume growth, raised FY guidance) shows no visible share loss yet

Take rate fell to 16.2bps in H1 2026 from 16.8bps in H1 2025. Management's 'expected volume tiering' explanation is plausible (large merchants structurally pay less per unit of volume as they scale, and this has been disclosed as a feature of the model for years) and is consistent with 21% CC revenue growth alongside 24% volume growth — a gap of modest magnitude, not a collapse. But it cannot yet be fully distinguished from the alternative (competitive discounting), especially given June 2026's explicit large-merchant pricing revision; this is the single most important swing factor for the long-run margin/multiple thesis

Digital net revenue growth improved to +13% YoY reported (+15% CC) in H1 2026 from Q1's record-low +9%/+13% CC, but remains the slowest pillar by a wide margin versus Unified Commerce (+25%/+27%) and Platforms (+37%/+40%). One half of reacceleration does not resolve whether Digital's largest content/subscription customers have permanently graduated to a lower blended take-rate tier, which would structurally cap group-level margin expansion even if group revenue growth holds

Adyen closed its first-ever acquisitions — Talon.One (€750mn, enterprise loyalty/promotions, 300+ global brands) and Orb ($335mn, usage-based billing) — on July 1, 2026, funded from available cash. This is a genuine strategic pivot after 15+ years of build-not-buy discipline. Co-CEO Uytdehaage is personally leading integration, concentrating executive bandwidth risk during a period of parallel CFO transition. Management guides the deals add ~1pp to 2026 revenue growth and cost ~1pp of margin (inclusive of one-time transaction costs); whether the strategic logic (extending Dynamic Identification pre/post-transaction) delivers durable cross-sell, or instead becomes a distraction/write-down risk, will not be knowable for several quarters

business.risk: Leadership transition concentrated in a 12-month window
business.description: Co-founder/Co-CEO Pieter van der Does stepped back from day-to-day leadership for health reasons in 2025, though he co-hosted the 13 August 2026 H1 earnings call alongside incoming interim CFO Hwa Tsao — a positive signal that he remains engaged in a visible, investor-facing capacity. CFO Ethan Tandowsky departs effective August 31, 2026 (announced May 2026) to pursue an opportunity outside fintech; Hwa Tsao (SVP Group Finance, joined Adyen November 2025, ex-ServiceNow/HP/Citigroup) becomes full-time interim CFO from September 1, 2026, with a permanent search ongoing via an external search firm. Gayathri Rajan was named Chief Product Officer effective July 1, 2026. This remains an unusually elevated concentration of C-suite change for a founder-culture company, now overlapping the company's first-ever M&A integration

financial.risk: Net income sensitivity to interest rates
financial.description: Finance income on own cash was €143.2mn in H1 2026, down slightly from €138.7mn in H1 2025 despite a larger average cash balance, reflecting the lower-rate environment (explicitly flagged in note 9 of the interim financials: 'decrease in interest earned on Cash held at central banks is primarily driven by a lower interest rate environment'); further ECB/Fed cuts would continue to compress this below-EBITDA income stream even as EBITDA itself grows strongly

H1 2026 net revenue growth was 19% reported vs. 21% CC — a ~2pp FX drag, consistent with prior periods; large USD-denominated North American and APAC-billed revenue creates translation risk each period, and the Orb acquisition consideration was USD-denominated

financial.risk: CapEx step-up to 7% of net revenue (new, elevated)
financial.description: Management raised 2026 CapEx guidance from 'up to 5%' to 7% of net revenue, citing a proactive pull-forward of 2027 datacenter spend to secure compute/storage availability and lock in pricing 'amid ongoing supply chain challenges.' Framed as temporary (returning to historical levels post-2026), but a genuine near-term free cash flow headwind; H1 2026 CapEx was already €64.1mn (5% of H1 net revenue) even before the back-half acceleration implied by the full-year 7% target, meaning H2 CapEx intensity will be materially higher than H1's

Purchase price allocation for Talon.One and Orb was still in progress as of the H1 2026 filing (accounting not finalized); goodwill will be booked on closing, introducing a new class of future impairment risk that did not exist in Adyen's balance sheet before July 2026

regulatory.description: Operating as a licensed credit institution (De Nederlandsche Bank) plus US and UK licenses, and now also a UAE Category II payments license, subjects Adyen to capital, AML/KYC, and prudential regulatory requirements across an expanding set of jurisdictions; auditor PwC (which reviewed the H1 2026 interim statements) reaches maximum permitted term after the FY2026 audit, requiring a new auditor appointment for FY2027

regulatory.risk: Payments regulation and interchange/scheme fee changes
regulatory.description: Regulatory shifts around interchange caps, open banking, payment method mandates, and (in the EU) progress toward a digital euro pilot require ongoing compliance investment and could reshape merchant economics across regions

Expanding use of AI-driven risk/identity decisioning (Dynamic Identification, Adyen Uplift, and the new Adyen Agentic product for AI-agent-initiated purchases) raises exposure to evolving AI and data-privacy regulation (EU AI Act, GDPR) as these tools scale into agentic-commerce use cases with partners including OpenAI

macro.description: Processed volume growth is tied to underlying consumer discretionary spending and e-commerce/retail volumes; H1 2026 volume grew 24% YoY, a reacceleration that suggests the macro backdrop was not a binding constraint in H1, but management has previously flagged 'continued macroeconomic uncertainty' framing for market-level volume growth

US tariff policy changes have prompted some customers to reassess where/how they grow and pivot to new regions — a secular tailwind for Adyen's multi-market platform but also a sign of macro-driven volatility in customer volumes

Beyond the direct P&L impact on finance income (already visibly compressing per note 9), broader rate cuts could reduce net income growth even as core operating (EBITDA) performance remains strong; net income growth (+13% YoY) continues to lag EBITDA growth (+18% YoY) in H1 2026, exactly this dynamic in evidence

growth_drivers: Continued 'land and expand' with existing large enterprise customers — roughly two-thirds of H1 2026 growth came from customers onboarded in 2024 and earlier, with disclosed share-of-wallet economics scaling from <20% (years 3-7) to >40% (after year 12)

Platforms pillar acceleration — fastest-growing pillar at +37% YoY reported/+40% CC in H1 2026, active business customers +51% YoY to 293K, 37 platform customers now processing >€1bn annually (up from 32); Orb acquisition extends this into usage-based billing infrastructure for AI/software companies

Unified Commerce structural advantage — +25%/+27% CC in H1 2026, 486 customers now processing at scale across channels, 838K transacting terminals (+27% YoY); Talon.One acquisition bridges online/offline loyalty, a gap standalone competitors cannot replicate

Intelligent Money Movement (IMM) — officially launched in H1 2026, unifying enterprise payments, liquidity management and payouts on a single platform; live customers include Etsy, Expedia, and Vinted, targeting travel-sector fund flows currently taking 4+ days to move from customer to supplier

Dynamic Identification / Adyen Uplift AI layer — now disclosing a quantified benefit (+0.9pp average conversion uplift by end of H1 2026); underpins both new acquisitions and the new Adyen Agentic product for AI-agent commerce

Adyen Agentic — new product suite (Agentic Feed + Agentic Cart) positioning Adyen as infrastructure for AI-agent-initiated purchases; early partners include OpenAI, American Express, Mastercard, Salesforce, Visa, and retailers ESW, Scheels, Sézane, SharkNinja

North America momentum — fastest-growing region in H1 2026 (+30% CC) and continued targeted hiring (249 net new joiners group-wide in H1 2026, bringing FTE to 5,020) to close the still-low market-share gap to Stripe
New market rail access — UAE Category II payments license and direct STET clearing membership in France, extending direct-rail access and settlement control

First-ever M&A: Talon.One (loyalty/promotions) and Orb (usage-based billing), closed July 1, 2026, expected to add ~1pp to 2026 net revenue growth and extend the platform's role before and after the transaction, not just at the point of sale

recent_developments.event: H1 2026 Shareholder Letter: net revenue €1,302.9mn (+19% reported/+21% CC); EBITDA €641.5mn (+18% YoY), margin 49% (50% excluding €6mn one-time acquisition transaction costs); net income €544.1mn (+13% YoY, including €143.2mn finance income on own cash); free cash flow €553.4mn (+17% YoY), 86% EBITDA conversion; processed volume €803.8bn (+24% YoY); take rate 16.2bps (down from 16.8bps in H1 2025, attributed to 'expected volume tiering'). Pillar detail: Digital €719.7mn +13%/+15% CC (still slowest, but improved from Q1's record-low +9%/+13% CC); Unified Commerce €417.7mn +25%/+27% CC; Platforms €165.5mn +37%/+40% CC. FTE reached 5,020 (+249 net new in H1). Management raised FY2026 net revenue growth guidance to 21-23% CC (from 20-22%, inclusive of the Talon.One/Orb contribution), reaffirmed the 55%+ EBITDA margin by 2028 target (2026 underlying margin in line with 2025, ~1pp lower including acquisitions), and raised 2026 CapEx guidance to 7% of net revenue (from 'up to 5%') to pull forward 2027 datacenter spend amid supply-chain constraints
recent_developments.significance: Strongest quarterly print since the Feb 2026 guidance cut; addresses two of the three 2026 overhangs (growth reacceleration, raised guidance) while leaving the take-rate and Digital-deceleration questions only partially resolved. The market reaction was decisively positive

recent_developments.event: Shares rose sharply on the H1 print — up roughly 16% on the day of results and further through the following two weeks, from ~€930.30 (9-Aug, pre-print) to ~€1,079.60 (28-Aug)
recent_developments.significance: First major positive catalyst of 2026 after a ~40%+ drawdown from Feb (margin-target push-out) through June (pricing-revision downgrades); Morgan Stanley upgraded to Overweight from Equal Weight with price target raised to €1,850 (from €1,205); Berenberg raised its target to €1,600 (from €1,700 pre-print, i.e. a smaller cut than feared) while maintaining Hold; other desks remained more cautious on the durability of the take-rate improvement

recent_developments.event: Adyen closed its first-ever acquisitions — Talon.One (€750mn, €69.8mn paid in shares) and Orb ($335mn, $33.2mn paid in shares) — funded from available cash; simultaneously named Gayathri Rajan Chief Product Officer (effective immediately) and confirmed SVP Group Finance Hwa Tsao as interim CFO effective Sept 1, 2026 ahead of Ethan Tandowsky's Aug 31 departure
recent_developments.significance: Consolidates the year's leadership and strategy transition into a single announcement: first-ever M&A plus a new CPO plus the interim CFO solution, with Co-CEO Uytdehaage personally leading integration. Deals expected to add ~1pp to 2026 revenue growth and cost ~1pp of margin

recent_developments.event: Gary Yang appointed APAC President effective August 1, 2026, succeeding retiring Warren Hayashi
recent_developments.significance: Routine regional leadership succession, adding to the broader pattern of management-team turnover in 2026, though APAC delivered solid H1 2026 growth (+23% reported/+26% CC)

recent_developments.event: Adyen revised elements of its pricing for large, high-volume enterprise merchants as competitive intensity increased; Berenberg and BNP Paribas/Exane downgraded the stock (Berenberg cut its price target to €1,095 from €1,950 and moved to Hold; BNP Paribas/Exane downgraded to Neutral, ~€890 target), citing pricing/take-rate risk
recent_developments.significance: First explicit evidence Adyen was proactively adjusting large-merchant pricing in response to competition; drove the stock to its 52-week low (~€772) before the H1 2026 print reversed sentiment. The H1 print's 16.2bps take rate and management's 'expected volume tiering' framing partially, but not fully, address the concern these downgrades raised

recent_developments.event: CFO Ethan Tandowsky announced resignation, effective August 31, 2026, to pursue an opportunity outside fintech; stock fell on the news
recent_developments.significance: Leadership transition risk; company reiterated no change to financial objectives; interim CFO solution (Hwa Tsao) confirmed at the July 1 update, and Tsao co-hosted the 13 August H1 earnings call alongside Co-founder/Co-CEO Pieter van der Does

recent_developments.event: Adyen entered definitive agreement to acquire Talon.One for €750mn (closed July 1, 2026); a separate agreement to acquire Orb followed on June 11, 2026 ($335mn, closed July 1, 2026)
recent_developments.significance: First acquisition announcements in company history

recent_developments.event: FY2025/H2 2025 results: full-year net revenue €2,364.2mn (+18% reported/+21% CC), full-year EBITDA margin 53% (H2 alone 55%); 2026 guidance issued at 20-22% CC net revenue growth (down from prior 'low-to-mid-20s' framing) and EBITDA margin 'broadly in line with 2025' rather than further expansion toward the (now-2028) 55%+ target
recent_developments.significance: Stock fell sharply (intraday declines as high as 17-20%) on the guidance disappointment; began the drawdown that troughed around €772 in June 2026 before the August reversal

items.target: 21-23% YoY on a constant currency basis, including the contribution of the Talon.One and Orb acquisitions (closed July 1, 2026)
items.vs_prior: raised from 20-22% CC (guidance given at Feb 2026 and reaffirmed at the May 2026 Q1 update)
items.notes: The raise is explicitly framed as inclusive of the acquisitions (~1pp contribution), but H1 organic performance (21% CC net revenue growth, 24% volume growth) also came in ahead of the prior guidance range on its own, supporting the increase

items.target: Above 55% by 2028 (long-term); 2026 underlying margin in line with 2025, but ~1 percentage point lower than 2025 including the acquisitions
items.vs_prior: maintained the 2028 long-term target; 2026 guidance refined to explicitly quantify the ~1pp acquisition dilution (inclusive of one-time transaction costs) that was not previously disclosed
items.notes: H1 2026 EBITDA margin was 49% reported (50% excluding one-time acquisition transaction costs), versus 50% in H1 2025 — the margin dilution from acquisitions and step-up in hiring/investment is already visible in the H1 print

items.vs_prior: raised sharply from 'up to 5% of net revenue' (prior long-standing guidance, reaffirmed as recently as the May 2026 Q1 update)
items.notes: Management frames this explicitly as accelerating 2027 datacenter capex into H2 2026 to secure compute/storage availability and lock in pricing 'amid ongoing supply chain challenges,' with CapEx expected to return to historical levels (~5%) post-2026. H1 2026 CapEx was already €64.1mn (5% of H1 net revenue), implying a much sharper H2 step-up to hit the full-year 7% target

Not explicitly re-addressed in the H1 2026 letter beyond the FY2026 guidance raise; sell-side models remain split, with the H1 print easing (but not eliminating) skepticism generated by the June 2026 pricing revision

guidance.management_commentary: The H1 2026 letter frames the half as 'strategically important' beyond the financial results, marking 'the next stage of our long-term strategy as we expand our role across the entire commerce journey' — from payments into loyalty (Talon.One), billing (Orb), and money movement (IMM). Management explicitly attributes the take-rate decline to 'expected volume tiering' rather than competitive pricing pressure, and highlights that customer concentration is diversifying (top 300 customers now ~60% of growth, down from >70% three years ago) as evidence of broadening, not narrowing, demand. On capital allocation: 'while organic growth remains our foundation, our strong balance sheet allows us to selectively deploy capital to accelerate our platform roadmap... We will continue to evaluate the optimal use of cash over time' — language that leaves the door open to further M&A. The earnings call was hosted by Co-founder/Co-CEO Pieter van der Does (his visible return to an investor-facing role, after stepping back for health reasons in 2025) alongside incoming interim CFO Hwa Tsao.

bull_case: H1 2026 delivered a clean, broad-based reacceleration — 21% CC net revenue growth, 24% volume growth, raised FY2026 guidance to 21-23% CC — directly refuting the market's worst fears from the Feb 2026 guidance cut and June 2026 pricing-revision downgrades, and Morgan Stanley's upgrade to Overweight (target raised to €1,850) reflects a genuine re-rating case

Platforms (+37%/+40% CC) and Unified Commerce (+25%/+27% CC) are both accelerating and now collectively ~45% of net revenue, diluting reliance on the slower Digital pillar over time even before Digital's own H1 improvement (+13%/+15% CC vs. Q1's +9%/+13% CC) is given credit

The take-rate decline (16.8 to 16.2bps) is consistent with, and plausibly explained by, benign volume-tiering as large customers scale rather than a broad-based competitive repricing — evidenced by revenue growth outpacing what a genuine take-rate collapse would produce, and by improving (not worsening) customer concentration

The Talon.One/Orb pivot and new IMM/Agentic products extend Adyen's role before and after the transaction (loyalty, billing, money movement, AI-agent commerce), widening the moat and the addressable wallet share per customer (disclosed at <20% in years 3-7 rising to >40% after year 12) well beyond simple payment-volume economics

Severe cumulative 2026 share-price reset (52-week range €772-€1,601) followed by a strong August reversal may still offer an attractive entry point if 21-23% FY2026 growth and margin targets prove durable, echoing the 2023-2024 pattern where a growth scare was followed by a sharp re-rating once results reaccelerated
bear_case: The take-rate decline to 16.2bps and the still-unresolved June 2026 large-merchant pricing revision mean the pricing-power question is not closed by one strong quarter — 'expected volume tiering' is management's own framing and cannot yet be independently verified against the alternative (competitive discounting to retain large accounts against Stripe and Braintree)

Digital, still the largest pillar at ~55% of revenue, remains the slowest-growing segment even after its H1 improvement; one half of reacceleration from a record-low Q1 print is not enough to conclude the largest pillar's growth ceiling has structurally lifted rather than merely bounced

CapEx guidance was raised sharply to 7% of net revenue (from 'up to 5%'), a genuine near-term free cash flow headwind; while framed as a one-year pull-forward, it is also consistent with a broader, less optimistic reading that AI-era infrastructure competition requires permanently higher capital intensity than the company's prior framework assumed

The first-ever M&A (Talon.One, Orb, combined ~$1.2bn) breaks with 15+ years of disciplined build-not-buy culture and management's own capital-allocation language ('we will continue to evaluate the optimal use of cash over time') signals more deals may follow — introducing new goodwill/integration risk to a company that has never before had to manage it, at precisely the moment its CFO is departing and a Co-CEO has only recently returned to a visible operating role after a health-related step-back

Leadership turnover remains unusually concentrated for a founder-culture company (CFO departure, new CPO, APAC president succession, and a Co-CEO health step-back all within roughly 12 months) — the H1 2026 results are strong, but the organization is absorbing an unusual amount of simultaneous change, and the permanent CFO search is still in progress
